summary: Latency-first fintech payments provider evaluating Redwood for low-tail-latency chat + rerank pipeline with aggressive cost targets; strong interest in batching/caching/quantization guidance and benchmark run.

notes: Workload: high-throughput payments notifications + conversational assistant for merchant support; spikes at EOD settlement windows.
Latency targets: 95th percentile chat latency <= 60ms (including model and network), 99th percentile budgeted at <=150ms during burst windows.
Throughput: baseline 500 requests/sec, burst to 5k requests/sec for short windows; average token length small (20-40 tokens) but many concurrent sessions.
Cost sensitivity: wants per-1M-token cost model; target ~50% reduction vs current self-hosted inference using float16 on T4s via better batching/quantization.
Model preferences: prefer open-weights Llama-family and Mistral variants; willing to accept 4-bit quantized variants if quality retained for reranking/chat.
Routing/fallback: must support automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant when Dedicated pool saturated; regional routing (us-east primary, failover us-west).
Caching needs: aggressive KV/prefix caching to accelerate repeated session turns; interested in Redwood's prefix cache warmup strategies and cache hit analytics.
Batching: want recommendations for dynamic batching vs fixed micro-batches during bursts; impact on tail latency is key.
Benchmark ask: Redwood to run 72-hour perf run with customer's three prompt families, compare A100 float16, A10G, and quantized T4-like profiles; provide cost curves and batch-size tradeoffs.
Security: must pass SOC2 and SAML SSO, require audit logs surfaced in Console; key management via AWS KMS preferred, retention policy 90 days for PII-adjacent telemetry.
Quote from CTO: 'We cannot let inference latency be the gating factor for settlement UX — sub-80ms tail is non-negotiable during normal hours.'
POC metric definitions: p95 latency, p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, model regression on 3 eval sets (accuracy, rerank NDCG).
Internal stakeholders: CTO (approval), Head of Platform (integration), SRE (benchmarks/peering), Legal (data residency).
Decision factors: 1) meet latency SLOs, 2) predictable burst behavior, 3) clear cost savings from Optimize recommendations, 4) security sign-offs.
